en.name: Pie crust, refrigerated
en.summary: Shop-bought refrigerated pie crust keeps 2 months at −18 °C (0 °F). In the fridge there is no separate timeline: the pack carries a use-by date and that date is the answer, because this is raw dough and it is sold chilled for a reason.
en.pantry: Not shelf-stable. Refrigerated pie crust is raw dough made with fat and water, sold chilled and never sterilised, so it belongs at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and must not be left on the counter. The two-hour rule applies once it comes out — one hour if the kitchen is above 32 °C (90 °F). In practice you want it cold anyway: warm pastry dough turns greasy and unrollable, and the whole trick of a flaky crust is solid fat suspended in cold dough.
en.fridge: No independent timeline is given, and none should be: go by the use-by date printed on the pack, which is the manufacturer's own statement about their own dough, and keep it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below in the unopened wrapper. Once the pack is opened the dough dries and darkens at the edges quickly, so rewrap what you do not use tightly in film and use it within a couple of days, or freeze it. If the pack has passed its date, do not judge raw pastry by eye — dough is one of the foods where the printed date is genuinely more reliable than your senses.
en.freezer: 2 months at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality. Freeze it in its wrapper inside a bag, or roll and line your tins first and freeze the lined tins, which is far more useful than freezing a slab. Kept continuously frozen it stays safe well beyond that window; what runs out is quality, as the fat and the flour dry and the dough cracks when you unroll it. Do not refreeze a crust you have already thawed on the counter.
en.thawing: Thaw it overnight in the fridge and unroll it while it is still cold but pliable — a cold-thawed crust handles far better than a warm one. Many recipes let you bake a lined tin straight from frozen, which avoids the problem entirely. Never thaw pastry on the counter.
spoilage: Grey, dry or darkened edges where the wrapper was open.
A sour or fermented smell when the pack is opened.
Any mould spot — throw the whole sheet out.
A sticky, slack dough that tears instead of rolling, usually from repeated warming and chilling.
tips: Go by the use-by date; with raw dough, that is the real answer.
Roll and line your tins, then freeze the lined tins rather than the dough slab.
Rewrap an opened sheet tightly in film — drying edges are the usual fault.
Keep it cold right up to the oven; warm pastry loses its flake.

faq.q: How long does refrigerated pie crust last?
faq.a: Go by the use-by date printed on the pack and keep it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. Frozen, it holds 2 months at −18 °C (0 °F).

faq.q: Can you freeze refrigerated pie crust?
faq.a: Yes, 2 months at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality. It is more useful to roll it, line your tins and freeze those than to freeze the slab.

faq.q: Can pie crust be left out at room temperature?
faq.a: No. It is raw chilled dough and follows the two-hour rule, one hour above 32 °C (90 °F). It also handles badly once it warms up.

zh.name: 冷藏派皮
zh.summary: 市售冷藏派皮在 −18 °C 冷凍可放 2 個月。冷藏則沒有另外的期限：包裝上有有效日期，那就是答案，因為這是生的麵團，它被冷藏販售是有原因的。
zh.pantry: 不能常溫存放。冷藏派皮是用油脂和水做的生麵團，冷藏販售、沒有經過滅菌，所以它該待在 4 °C 以下，不能擺在檯面上。拿出來之後適用兩小時原則，廚房超過 32 °C 時只有一小時。實務上你本來就要它冰：麵團一暖就出油、擀不動，而酥脆派皮的全部訣竅，就是固體油脂懸浮在冰冷麵團裡。
zh.fridge: 這裡不另外給期限，也不該給：請以包裝上印的有效日期為準，那是製造商對自家麵團的說法；未拆封、放 4 °C 以下保存。拆封之後，麵團邊緣很快會變乾變深，所以沒用完的請用保鮮膜緊緊重新包好，兩三天內用掉，或直接冷凍。如果已經過了日期，不要用肉眼去判斷生麵團——派皮正是那種「印製日期比你的感官更可靠」的食品。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 2 個月品質最好。連原包裝一起裝袋冷凍，或者先擀好、鋪進模具，再把鋪好的模整個冷凍，那比冷凍一塊麵團實用得多。只要全程沒退冰，超過這個期限仍然安全；先用完的是品質——油脂和麵粉變乾，攤開的時候就會裂。在檯面上退冰過的派皮不要再冷凍。
zh.thawing: 放冷藏隔夜解凍，趁它還冰、但已經有彈性的時候攤開——冷藏解凍的派皮比回溫過的好處理太多。很多食譜可以直接把鋪好的模從冷凍送進烤箱，那就完全避開了這個問題。絕對不要在檯面上退冰。
spoilage: 包裝開口處的邊緣發灰、變乾或顏色變深。
打開包裝聞起來發酸或有發酵味。
只要出現一個霉點就整張丟掉。
麵團變得黏軟、一擀就破，通常是反覆回溫又冰回去造成的。
tips: 以有效日期為準；生麵團的真正答案就是那個日期。
先擀好鋪進模具，冷凍鋪好的模，不要冷凍一整塊麵團。
拆封後用保鮮膜重新包緊——邊緣變乾是最常見的毛病。
一路冰到進烤箱為止；派皮一暖就沒有酥層了。

faq.a: 以包裝上的有效日期為準，並放在 4 °C 以下。冷凍的話 −18 °C 下 2 個月。
可以，−18 °C 下 2 個月品質最好。與其冷凍一整塊，不如先擀好鋪進模具再冷凍。
不行。它是冷藏的生麵團，適用兩小時原則，超過 32 °C 只有一小時。而且一回溫就很難操作。
